decisions.reason: As a flagship tied to the firm's stated strategic direction, this crate carries high public commitment and sunk development effort, which makes management likely to persist unless failure is unmistakable.

A multi-model foldable container line with its own product page fits the core reusable-packaging business and likely embodies substantial tooling and commercialization investment, encouraging continued support.
Although less visibly promoted, a stackable crate line with several models is close to the firm's established offering, so moderate sunk costs and portfolio fit favor retention.

This pallet line appears less central than the flagship products, but its multiple models and relevance to the core logistics-packaging range still make managers inclined to keep it rather than admit a weak launch.

The spill-retention pallet seems more niche and lost promotional prominence after launch, yet the initial standalone presentation and likely product-specific investment still bias management toward continuing it.

This pallet variant looks specialized and less central to the firm's announced direction, but because it was publicly introduced and likely shares production assets with the pallet business, management is still slightly more likely to retain it than withdraw it.
